Optimizing Sleep Hygiene

Quality rest is driven by your internal body clock and the regulation of sleep-related brain chemicals. Experts note that pre-sleep routines significantly impact your ability to fall and stay asleep.

Key disruptive habits include:

  • Screen Time: Blue light and engaging content can suppress melatonin.
  • Caffeine Intake: Beverages like coffee or tea can block sleep-inducing chemicals for hours.
  • Mental Overload: Ruminating on daily tasks keeps the brain alert.
  • Dietary Choices: Heavy meals and alcohol late at night interfere with physical comfort and sleep cycles.
  • Irregular Scheduling: Inconsistent bedtimes disrupt your circadian rhythm.

To improve sleep, experts suggest establishing a consistent routine, avoiding caffeine six hours before bed, and unplugging devices 30 minutes prior to sleep. If you experience persistent issues like snoring or excessive daytime fatigue, consult a healthcare professional.
